caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 54 of 1971
lawyer:
MA Wahab, Advocate------For the Appellant
Khondker AM Mohsenuddin, Advocate------For the Respondent No.1
parties:
Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Chairman, Bangladesh Railway Board -----Appellant
Vs.
Commerce Bank Ltd and Ors ----- Respondents
full_judgment: 2. The respondent being plaintiff instituted the aforesaid Money Suit on the allegation that defendant No. 1 being a businessman dealing in whole-sale agency business maintained a current account being No. C/A 396 with the plaintiff bank. On 12.4.68 defendant No. 1 produced a railway receipt commonly known as RR being No. 946167 dated 10.4.68 signifying despatch of 225 bags of Massors weighing about 511.30 seers with bags from Mobarakganj Railway Station to Ambikapur Railway Station and requested the plaintiff to purchase the same. The plaintiff purchased the RR and advanced an amount of Taka 11,956.06 which was to be the value of the goods sent under the RR in the bill dated 12.4.68. The RR was duly endorsed in favour of the plaintiff. Again on 23.4.68 the defendant No. 1 produced another RR being No. 946183 dated 21.4.68 signifying the dispatch of 225 bags of Massors weighing about 500 mds, with bags from Mobarakganj railway station to Ambikapur railway station. The plaintiff accordingly purchased the RR and again advanced an amount of Taka 12,156.26 which was the value of the goods sent under RR in the bill dated 22.4.68 and the RR was duly endorsed in favour of the plaintiff. Both the aforesaid bills were purchased at the risk and responsibility to the defendant No. 1 as per instruments embodied in the documents. After purchasing the bill they were sent to defendant No. 5 duly endorsed in their favour for collection on 12.4.68 and 23.4.68 respectively and the drawee of the bill is one Jitendra Nath Saha. Instruction of the plaintiff to defendant No. 5 was also embodied in the document. Subsequently, the plaintiff received the bills along with the RR as the same were not released by the drawee. Defendant No. 5 however cancelled the endorsement made on the back of the said document. After correspondence plaintiff was enlightened by defendant No. 5 with regard to the cancellation of the endorsement by him. On receipt of the return of the bills by letter dated 18.6.68 the plaintiff enquired about the matter to the station master Ambikapur railway station defendant No. 4 to let him know the position of the consignment of the RR and in return defendant No. 4 by letter No. M/4468 dated 19.6.68 informed that the consignment in question was not in his possession. Thereafter the plaintiff made personal enquiries but the defendant No. 4 could not give any satisfactory reply about the goods. The plaintiff also made enquiry about the matter to defendant No. 3 but he also could not give any information. Then the plaintiff by letter dated 11.7.68 requested the Chief Commercial Manager (Claims) of defendant No. 2 to enquire about the matter and arrange delivery of the goods but without any reply and then finding no other alternative the plaintiff served a legal notice upon the defendant No. 2 on 5.10.68 but without any result. The plaintiff also sent a telegram on 12.1.68 to defendant No. 2 for redress of his grievance but no reply came from him. On demand for payment of the dues defendant No. 1 assured co-operation with the plaintiff for adjustment of the liability but it stood as assurance only without any payment. The total claim of the plaintiff was Taka 25,499.25 together with interest at the rate of 9-1/2% per annum as per rules and practice. The further case of the plaintiff was that by reason of purchase of the bills and for that matter the RR had always interest and control over the goods and nobody could take the goods without payment. Defendant Nos. 2-4 are bound as carrier either to deliver the goods or to account for the goods to the plaintiff or in default pay value thereof with interest and charges, etc. It is further asserted by the plaintiff that the consignment under the RR were booked on 10.4.68 and 21.4.68 and the same were supposed to reach Ambikapur railway station via Poradah, Kushtia and Rajbari station on or about 18.4.68 and 19.4.68 respectively and ought to have been delivered on or about 28 or 29th or 30th April, 1968 but not only the goods were not delivered but also the defendant Nos. 2-4 could not give out any trace of the goods, and as such these defendants are required to make good the loss of the plaintiff.
